9. Bleeding from artery is more dangerous than that from vein, give reason.
Ans:- Arteries carry blood under high pressure; bleeding is rapid and can cause severe blood loss. Veins carry blood under
low pressure; bleeding is slower and less dangerous.
10. How is angiogram prepared?
Ans:- A contrast dye is injected into the blood vessels. X-rays are then taken to visualize the vessels and detect blockages or
abnormalities.

17. Wall ventricle is highly muscular or thicker than the wall of auricle. Why?
Ans:- Ventricles pump blood out of the heart against resistance (arterial pressure), so they need thick muscular walls.
Auricles only receive blood, so their walls are thin.
18. Arteries are deeply seated inside the muscles but veins are superficial. Why?
Ans:- Arteries are under high pressure; muscles protect them from injury. Veins are under low pressure; they can safely be
located near the skin. So, Arteries are deeply seated inside the muscles but veins are superficial.
19. Blood coagulates slower or does not coagulate in hemophilic person. Why?
Ans:- Hemophilia is due to deficiency of clotting factors (like factor VIII or IX), so coagulation is delayed or absent.
20. When any part of the body is injured, the bleeding stops after a while. Why?
Ans:- Platelets aggregate at the injury site forming a clot. Fibrin threads reinforce the clot, stopping bleeding.
